sections.html:
Cedar City is the largest city in Iron County, in southwestern Utah, about 250 miles south of Salt Lake City and 170 miles north of Las Vegas along Interstate 15. It sits above 5,600 feet in Cedar Valley, with St. George about 50 miles southwest. Zion, Bryce Canyon and Cedar Breaks are all a day trip away.

The population was 35,235 in 2020 and is estimated at 41,871 for July 2025, with 11,824 households and 12,723 housing units at the last full count. The median age is 26.2, a reflection of Southern Utah University. With that many students come plenty of rentals, a point for any landlord weighing a sale. Local demand follows the school term and the festival season, so choose a closing date with those swings in mind.

The climate is semi-arid, with about 11 inches of precipitation a year and about 47.8 inches of snow. January highs average 42.8 degrees and lows 18.0, July highs average 91.0, and the record low is minus 26. Exteriors take a beating across that spread. Repeated freezing and thawing splits driveways and stucco, dry summers fade roofing, and cold nights strain older plumbing and water heaters. Anyone touring in winter quickly notices insulation, windows and the heating bill.

  • Roof condition after heavy snow seasons
  • Exposed pipes and outdoor spigots
  • Cracked concrete and stucco
  • Heating system age and efficiency

Empty houses need care in both seasons, since pipes can freeze in winter and weeds and dust pile up in summer.

City Hall is at 10 North Main Street, open 8 am to 5 pm. The City Council meets Wednesdays at 5:30 pm and streams on YouTube, except on the fifth Wednesday of a month. The city offers a water usage app called MY360 that lets residents view their water use, which helps when you close out an account.

Travel runs on Interstate 15. A Union Pacific branch skirts the west side, the regional airport has Delta Connection service, and the city has its own bus system.

sections.h2: How Iron County assesses and bills property tax
sections.html:
Cedar City homes are valued and billed by Iron County, whose offices are at 68 South 100 East in Parowan. Each property is judged on its condition and owner as of January 1, using cost, income and market methods. Reach the Assessor at 435-477-8310.

Iron County property tax calendar
StepTiming
Notice of Valuation and Taxes mailedAround July 22
Board of Equalization appeals dueSeptember 15, 5:00 PM (or 45 days after the notice, if later)
Property tax notices mailedAround November 1
Tax payment due statewideNovember 30

Utah taxes a primary residence on 55 percent of value, with the cut under Utah Code 59-2-103 capped at one acre of land per unit. Missing November 30 makes the bill delinquent on December 1, and years of nonpayment can send a parcel to a tax sale. Owe back taxes? Speak to the treasurer before listing.

Start an appeal with the Iron County Auditor at 435-477-8333. The Board of Equalization normally meets from late September to early October. Because the assessed figure is presumed right, bring solid proof of a lower market value: recent comparable sales, an appraisal, or a documented mistake in the county record.

Evidence is easier to gather in summer. Photograph any defects, save repair quotes and print your closing statement if you bought recently.

Pay by November 30 even if the appeal is still open. Should the house sell meanwhile, let the buyer's side know, so escrow can direct any refund.

sections.h2: Selling a student or seasonal rental
sections.html:
Southern Utah University reported a fall 2025 headcount of 15,825 students, up 2.47 percent from the year before, including more than 3,691 fully online students. Landlords near campus feel that in both directions: demand is steady, and turnover wears houses down. Events such as the Utah Shakespeare Festival and athletics bring visitors too, and rental demand can rise and fall with the term and the summer.

Selling a rental begins with the lease. One that outlasts your target closing usually stays in force, so note its end date, the rent and any deposit you hold. A buyer keeping the tenant needs those figures, while a buyer wanting the house empty needs to know how much notice you can give. Get the terms on paper before signing a contract.

After each tenant moves out, walk the house and record any damage. Turnover repairs are why many of these houses linger. Cash sales do not require you to fix them, though a plain list lets the buyer price the work fairly.

Notices arrive around November 1 with payment due November 30, so a fall or winter closing can collide with a bill. Check with the title company soon on whether this year is paid, and keep the notice handy. Behind on payments? Watch December 1. Get a precise payoff from the treasurer before taking an offer, and let escrow clear the balance from your proceeds.

The calendar matters for appeals too. Valuation notices show up around July 22 and September 15 is a firm cutoff, so if you think the value is high, act in late summer instead of waiting for the tax bill.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale skip?
sections.html:
Cedar City sellers often decide on a cash sale during a short window, such as the weeks between a tenant leaving and the first hard freeze. Because nobody is waiting on loan approval, the schedule comes down to title work and how quickly any payoff letters arrive.

A cash sale drops the lender appraisal and any list of buyer repair requests. The process is short.

  1. Tell the buyer about the house, plus any tenants, liens or repairs.
  2. An offer comes back and you accept or decline.
  3. The title company checks the record and lines up payoffs.
  4. Closing happens on your chosen day and you collect payment.

Before calling, locate your most recent Iron County tax notice, any tenant's lease dates and your mortgage payoff figures. Mention it if the house sat empty over winter, since a buyer will check for freeze damage.

sections.h2: What Cedar City sellers usually face
sections.html:
Typical Cedar City sellers hold an aging rental, a dated house, or a place inherited from a relative out of state. A cash sale suits them because no lender is involved and no repair list arrives.

  • Student and seasonal rentals with turnover damage
  • Houses with older roofs, windows and heating systems
  • Inherited property where heirs live in other states
  • Vacant houses that sit empty through a cold winter

What they generally want is one firm closing date rather than months of showings. Hand over lease dates and rent details early so move-out terms are written down.

faqs.q: What county is Cedar City in, and who sets my property value?
faqs.a: Iron County. Its Assessor works from 68 South 100 East in Parowan and can be reached at 435-477-8310.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Cedar City property value?
faqs.a: By 5:00 PM on September 15, or 45 days after your valuation notice is mailed if that date is later. Call the Auditor at 435-477-8333 to file.

faqs.q: What is the property tax due date in Cedar City?
faqs.a: The due date is November 30. Notices go out around November 1, and a balance left unpaid is delinquent on December 1.
It had 35,235 residents in 2020 and an estimated 41,871 in July 2025, making it the largest city in Iron County.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in Cedar City with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, whether the tenants stay or go. Give lease dates and rent details early so the closing date and move-out terms are written down.
